summary.text: A previously healthy 37-year-old man presented with one week of sudden, rapidly worsening painless bilateral vision loss, was afebrile and had a normal neurological examination. Fundoscopy showed bilateral cotton wool spots, arteriolar narrowing, vascular sheathing and hemorrhages; fluorescein angiography showed retinal vasculitis with occlusive retinal arteriolitis and OCT showed macular edema with subretinal fluid.

He met 2019 EULAR/ACR criteria for SLE with a score of 14, SLEDAI-2K 12 points, ANA positive at 1:1280, with a skin biopsy showing features of subacute cutaneous lupus; Behçet disease, ANCA vasculitis, sarcoidosis and Sjögren syndrome were ruled out.

He received pulsed intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, hydroxychloroquine, cyclophosphamide and intravitreal bevacizumab, with partial clinical improvement and SLEDAI-2K of 8 points at one-month follow-up. Table 3 and the narrative disagree on his presentation visual acuity, visual fields and color vision.

summary.text: A 33-year-old woman had a two-year rash that appeared during pregnancy, two generalized tonic-clonic seizures 15 days before presentation, and two weeks of sudden, painless dimness of vision more diminished on the left. Examination showed erythematous crusted rashes, best corrected acuity 6/36 right and counting fingers left, bilateral cotton wool spots and impaired left-eye visual fields and color vision.

She met 2019 EULAR/ACR criteria for SLE with a score of 23, SLEDAI-2K 18 points (severe flare); fluorescein angiography showed retinal vasculitis and OCT showed cystoid macular edema and subretinal fluid. ANA was positive at 1:320, rheumatoid factor was positive at a high titer and urine culture grew E. coli.

She received pulsed intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, hydroxychloroquine, cyclophosphamide and intravitreal bevacizumab, with partial clinical improvement and SLEDAI-2K of 8 points at one-month follow-up.

summary.text: A 19-year-old woman with six months of intermittent low-grade fever, malar and ear rashes, joint pain and oral ulcers was diagnosed with SLE by a dermatologist and started on hydroxychloroquine 200 mg and prednisolone 20 mg daily. She was admitted with a two-month history of progressive, painless bilateral dimness of vision that worsened with a left relative afferent pupillary defect; prednisolone 60 mg did not improve her condition and she was referred to rheumatology.

Examination showed best corrected acuity 6/60 right and counting fingers at one foot left, active vasculitis with cotton wool spots and hemorrhage, and profuse vitreal and pre-retinal hemorrhage in the left eye; fluorescein angiography showed retinal vasculitis and OCT showed increased retinal thickness with intraretinal fluid. She met 2019 EULAR/ACR criteria with a score of 14 and SLEDAI-2K of 8 points.
She received pulsed intravenous methylprednisolone, oral prednisolone, hydroxychloroquine and cyclophosphamide, with partial clinical improvement and SLEDAI-2K of 8 points at one-month follow-up.
